key_insight: Binary silver labels from EHRs can be used directly in weakly supervised phenotyping, and Binary PheNorm turns them into stronger phenotype scores without requiring EM calibration.
clinical_relevance: This offers a practical way to build scalable computable phenotypes when binary indicators like medication mentions or lab thresholds are available and chart review is not.
method: Extends PheNorm to use binary silver labels directly in the denoising regression step.
Adds an optional lasso-regularized version for high-dimensional EHR data.
Can combine binary and count-based silver labels into one model.
evidence_signal: In simulations and two EHR phenotyping examples, Binary PheNorm improved discrimination, with AUC rising to 0.891-0.892 for anaphylaxis and 0.805-0.819 for acute pancreatitis.
watch_item: Performance depends on the informativeness of the binary silver label, so poor-quality indicators may limit gains or require careful validation.
paper_title: Using binary silver labels in electronic health records-based computable phenotyping algorithms
